title: Haywood Henry and the Dukes
summary: He tells of sax player Haywood Henry, who subbed with Ellington, and of his own group The Dukes playing weddings, where Henry praises his riffs.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: It’s funny that I’m going to skip forward, for many years there was a great sax player named Haywood Henry, [inaudible] for Erskine Hawkins.

He actually used to sub in Duke’s band sometimes when Harry wasn’t there. But Haywood told me like the first time he ever did it, you know he went in there and was like what’s going to happen, they’re all like, this could be a drag. And Haywood got on the bandstand and he started playing and someone said in the back, you could hear someone say, “All right everything’s going to be all right. So what was I telling the story about? I’m losing it. Oh, oh, the riff, the riff. So anyway, we used to do a lot of gigs. I have a seven piece group called The Dukes, I’ll get you a CD and stuff. And sometimes when they couldn’t afford the whole eight piece group we’d do like a quintet or a sextet, because I had a great front line of like Haywood and me and this great trumpet player, Irvin Stokes, probably like Richard Wyands playing piano, and guys like Earl May on bass, these things like that, so it’s a great band. We’re playing a wedding on a boat — and the people who hire you at weddings, it was like this is what you’re going to get. I

never try to fool them to think they’re going to get top 40. And there was people who really wanted it. So three of us are up there, horn players, and we’re playing, someone’s taking a solo, we set riffs, so I set a few riffs. And so one time after Haywood heard a few of the riffs I was setting, he always gave me a ride home with his wife Mil. And he said, “Boy you sound real good, man. And you know those colored riffs.”

You know you learned those colored riffs. He always liked to say things like that too, that just would make me laugh. Some stories he told over and over again, because he knew I loved them. He was amazing man.
